life_story.answer: I started in electrical engineering and began my career in service engineering, where I learned to troubleshoot real-world problems systematically. I later moved into data science through training and an internship, and then into AI and data science roles. Today, I build practical AI prototypes using Python, LLMs and RAG, while continuing to improve my software engineering fundamentals by building and testing projects.

superpower.answer: My strongest point is turning a vague idea into a practical first version. I break problems into smaller steps, test an approach with the tools available, and then check what actually works. I try to be honest about the difference between a quick prototype and something that is production-ready.

growth_areas.answer: The top three areas I want to improve are software engineering fundamentals, production reliability, and explaining technical trade-offs clearly. I want to become more independent at writing maintainable code, get better at testing failure cases, and explain why a solution fits the actual problem. I treat these as ongoing areas of practice.

misconception.answer: I cannot confidently speak for what all my coworkers think, so I would not want to invent a misconception. When I am focused on solving something, people may see the implementation before they see all the checking and learning happening behind it. I try to make my assumptions and progress more visible as I work.

boundaries.answer: I push my limits by choosing a concrete problem that is a little beyond what I already know and breaking it into smaller experiments. I use documentation and AI tools to speed up learning, but I still verify the output, test edge cases, and understand what I ship. That lets me explore new areas without pretending to know everything already.

projects.answer: I've worked on several projects: a Renewal Intelligence Engine with churn prediction using Random Forest and a RAG pipeline; a RAG assistant using Python, FastAPI, LangChain, FAISS, Hugging Face embeddings and Streamlit; and an e-commerce website project. These showcase my work with Python, LLMs, RAG, and machine learning.
